exposure: delivery type (normal vaginal delivery with episiotomy, uncomplicated cesarean section)
outcome: strength and endurance of pelvic floor muscles (PFM)
cohort: Primigravida females who had either a normal vaginal delivery with episiotomy or an uncomplicated cesarean section were included.
finding: Women who underwent uncomplicated cesarean delivery had better outcomes regarding pelvic floor muscle dysfunction, electrical activity, strength, endurance, and vaginal pressure compared to those who had a normal vaginal delivery with episiotomy.
mod_finding: Uncomplicated cesarean section was associated with lower severity of pelvic floor dysfunction compared to normal vaginal delivery with episiotomy, suggesting VDE may cause PFM injury.
